item.text:
**Bottom line**
- Mixed, leaning yes on technocratic staffing and continuity, but only weak evidence that Modi fully empowered independent economic professionals rather than using them inside a politically managed coalition state.

**Accepted Claims**
- [India’s Modi prevails over allies in cabinet line-up](https://theprint.in/india/indias-modi-prevails-over-allies-in-cabinet-line-up/2126130/) — Reuters via ThePrint — 11 Jun 2024 — Modi kept the finance ministry and other senior economic portfolios in the same hands after the election setback, which is the clearest evidence of continuity in economic staffing rather than a turnover to obvious loyalists. Questions: 5B.2; 4B.10.

- [Indian government appoints members for new finance panel](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/indian-government-appoints-members-for-new-finance-panel-3287402) — Reuters via Investing.com — 30 Jan 2024 — The government named a technocratic Finance Commission team including former expenditure officials, a policy executive, SBI’s chief economic adviser, and economist Arvind Panagariya as chair, which supports the view that Modi relied on experienced economic professionals in major fiscal institutions. Questions: 5B.2.

- [India’s budget keeps spending in check; sees modest increase in revenue](https://theprint.in/india/indias-budget-keeps-spending-in-check-sees-modest-increase-in-revenue/1949061/) — Reuters via ThePrint — 1 Feb 2024 — The interim budget stayed fiscally tight despite the election year, raised capital expenditure, and avoided a classic pre-poll giveaway, which is positive evidence that the economic team was allowed to pursue longer-term fiscal management. Questions: 5B.2; 5B.1.

- [Shri Sanjay Malhotra takes over as RBI Governor](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=59281) — Reserve Bank of India — 11 Dec 2024 — Modi’s government appointed Sanjay Malhotra, a career IAS officer with finance, taxation, IT, and revenue experience, as RBI governor; that is strong technocratic evidence, though it is still a bureaucratic rather than independent-economist appointment. Questions: 5B.2.

- [India’s Modi spends billions on jobs, key allies in first budget after election](https://theprint.in/india/indias-modi-spends-billions-on-jobs-key-allies-in-first-budget-after-election/2187546/) — Reuters via ThePrint — 23 Jul 2024 — The first post-election budget directed large sums to jobs, rural programs, and coalition-partner states explicitly to win back voters and retain political support, which is counterevidence that economic policy was insulated from short-term political bargaining. Questions: 5B.2; 5B.1.

- [India’s Modi faces delicate balancing act in post-election budget](https://theprint.in/india/indias-modi-faces-delicate-balancing-act-in-post-election-budget/2186495/) — Reuters via ThePrint — 23 Jul 2024 — Reuters described the budget as balancing fiscal prudence with disgruntled voters and coalition demands, showing that economic decisionmaking was constrained by political management rather than purely professional autonomy. Questions: 5B.2; 5B.1.

**Search gap**
- I did not find reliable 2024 reporting showing Modi filling top economic posts with family members or business partners.
- I also did not find strong direct evidence about the degree of day-to-day empowerment these professionals had inside the PMO; the reporting is strongest on appointment continuity and institutional staffing, weaker on autonomy.
